name: Asnah
overview: Asnah is a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role was connected to the religious duties of the Levitical community during the post-exilic period. Scripture identifies him specifically in the context of temple service, highlighting his contribution to the worship life of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Asnah likely means 'thornbush' or 'he who belongs to Nah.' This proper name, recorded in Ezra 2:50, is not indicated as being given directly by God but reflects a common Hebrew naming practice of the time.
familyAndRelationships: Asnah is identified as a descendant of Levi, establishing his Levitical heritage and qualifying him for temple service. Beyond this tribal connection, Scripture does not record any additional family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Asnah's significance lies in his role as a temple servant among the Levites, emphasizing the restoration of proper worship following the exile. His mention in Ezra 2:50 underlines the careful record-keeping and the reestablishment of the Levitical priesthood and temple service in the post-exilic community. Through his service, Asnah contributed to the continuity of God's covenantal worship among His people.
